result.summary: The street is a wide two-lane roadway with on-street parking on both sides and sidewalks present. There are no visible marked crosswalks or pedestrian safety infrastructure, and the presence of an elevated highway structure creates a less hospitable environment for walking.

hazards.name: Lack of marked crossings
hazards.description: No designated crossing points are visible for pedestrians along this stretch of road, forcing mid-block crossings.

hazards.name: Visual obstructions from parked cars
hazards.description: Continuous on-street parking blocks sightlines between drivers and pedestrians who might attempt to cross.

interventions.title: Install High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Add marked crosswalks with high-visibility paint at regular intervals or intersections to define pedestrian space.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Install curb extensions at potential crossing points to reduce crossing distance and improve visibility by moving pedestrians past the line of parked cars.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces near intersections or crossing points to improve sightlines between drivers and pedestrians.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment is located under a large elevated highway structure, featuring a wide sidewalk separated from a parking and access area by a row of bollards. The space is dominated by massive concrete pillars that create significant visual obstructions and a dark, cavernous atmosphere lacking clear crossing infrastructure.

hazards.name: Visual Obstructions
hazards.description: Large concrete support pillars block sightlines between pedestrians and vehicles moving through the parking and access area.
hazards.location_in_image: Throughout the mid-ground under the bridge deck.

hazards.name: Poor Lighting
hazards.description: The area under the elevated highway is naturally dark, which reduces visibility for all road users and can decrease perceived safety.
hazards.location_in_image: Entire area under the bridge structure.

interventions.title: Pedestrian-Scale Lighting
interventions.description: Install high-quality, uniform lighting under the bridge deck to improve visibility and security for pedestrians.

interventions.title: Marked Crosswalks and Wayfinding
interventions.description: Define clear pedestrian paths across the asphalt area with high-visibility markings and signage to organize movement.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment is dominated by industrial land use and a large overpass, featuring a wide roadway with significant pavement damage. While a sidewalk exists on the right, the left side lacks formal pedestrian infrastructure, and the overall design prioritizes vehicle movement and parking over pedestrian safety.

hazards.name: Severe Pavement Degradation
hazards.description: Large potholes and cracking in the center of the roadway create trip hazards and may cause vehicles to swerve unexpectedly.
hazards.location_in_image: Center foreground and mid-ground of the roadway.

hazards.name: Incomplete Sidewalk Network
hazards.description: The lack of a paved sidewalk on the left side forces pedestrians to walk on uneven gravel or in the roadway near traffic.
hazards.location_in_image: Left side of the image, adjacent to the overpass supports.

hazards.name: Sightline Obstructions
hazards.description: A continuous line of parked vehicles on the left side of the street obscures pedestrians from the view of oncoming drivers.

interventions.title: Roadway Resurfacing
interventions.description: Repair and resurface the roadway to eliminate potholes and provide a safe, even surface for all users.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Construction
interventions.description: Install a continuous, ADA-compliant concrete sidewalk on the left side of the street to provide a dedicated pedestrian space.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions and High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install curb extensions at intersections to reduce crossing distances and use high-visibility markings to clearly define pedestrian paths.

result.summary: The intersection features basic pedestrian infrastructure including sidewalks and a faded zebra crosswalk, controlled by a stop sign. However, the lack of high-visibility markings, poor pavement condition, and absence of traffic calming measures like curb extensions limit the overall safety of the environment.

hazards.name: Faded Crosswalk
hazards.description: The painted zebra markings are significantly worn, making the crossing less visible to motorists.

hazards.name: Degraded Pavement
hazards.description: Cracks and uneven surfaces in the roadway can pose a trip hazard or affect vehicle handling.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalk
interventions.description: Repaint the crossing with high-visibility thermoplastic markings to improve driver compliance and pedestrian safety.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Construct bulb-outs at the intersection corners to shorten the pedestrian crossing distance and slow turning traffic.

interventions.title: Pavement Resurfacing
interventions.description: Repair the cracked and uneven roadway surface to ensure a smooth and safe path for all users.
